samples.summary: Large hardening effort (numeric attribute bands + paginator loop bound) rides along on an issue about list-level subtrees
samples.evidence: Issue #1050 and its task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260908-docs-list-level-subtree-todo.md) scope the change to "changing a list item's level carries its nested children": the plan lists `model/list-level.ts`, threading `siblings` through the three `forEachBlockInSelection`, routing the entry points, tests, and the docs.md note. The `listLevel` band is a defensible extension of that (its own "Review follow-ups" section records it). But `model/row-height.ts`, `model/numeric-attrs.ts` (fontSize / lineHeight / cell padding / inline image size), the `crdt-attrs.ts` lineHeight band, the `table-layout.ts` re-normalization and `pagination.ts`'s new `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` clipping appear nowhere in the issue, the plan, or the follow-up list, and are a distinct concern (untrusted-geometry DoS in the paginator) with its own user-visible behavior change (a table row is now clipped past 200 pages, and stored heights above 10000px / font sizes above 400pt are silently discarded). Bundling it makes the list-level fix and a pagination/geometry policy change one reviewable unit and one revert unit.
samples.severity_reason: cost stays inside the codebase's own reviewability; the shipped behavior still satisfies the issue

samples.summary: The CRDT attribute-decode contract change and the paginator clipping bound are recorded in docs.md rather than in the canonical docs for those subsystems
samples.evidence: docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md:86 §"Attribute encoding contract (block style)" is the canonical statement of what the shared codec emits and what the reader inverts ("a *finite* number for each of `lineHeight` / `marginTop` / ..."). This change tightens exactly that contract — `lineHeight` is now dropped unless it is in `(0, 20]`, and `fontSize`, cell `padding`, image size and `rowHeights` gain bands at both read boundaries — yet that doc is untouched and the new rules are written into docs/design/docs/docs.md:190-232 instead. Likewise the row-split loop lives in docs/design/docs/docs-pagination.md §Table Row Splitting and docs/design/docs/tables/docs-table-row-splitting.md, whose Goals say rows "render continuously" and whose Non-Goals do not mention clipping; the new `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` clip (content past 200 pages is discarded) is recorded only in docs.md. Per CONTRIBUTING/design discipline the repo folds a change into the canonical subsystem doc rather than describing it from a neighbouring one.

samples.summary: The new normalizers are not used at the third boundary (the clipboard sanitizer), which keeps its own hand-rolled listLevel clamp and admits any finite rowHeight / fontSize / padding
samples.evidence: The change centralizes the bands (`normalizeListLevel`, `normalizeRowHeight`, `normalizeFontSize`, `normalizeCellPadding`, `isPaintableImageSize`) and states the rule as "band the value where it enters the model", applying it at `crdt-tree.ts` and `YorkieDocStore`. `clipboard.ts` is the remaining place values enter the model: it now imports `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` but re-implements the clamp inline (`Math.min(MAX_LIST_LEVEL, Math.max(0, Math.trunc(level)))`, line 349-351) instead of calling `normalizeListLevel`, and its table/inline sanitizers pass `asNumber` (finite-only, clipboard.ts:69) straight through for `rowHeights` (line 298), cell `padding` (line 235) and marker/inline `fontSize` (lines 141, 211) — so a pasted `1e9` font size or padding is materialized and written back to the CRDT unbanded. The diff and design doc acknowledge this ("the clipboard sanitizer admits any finite number") and answer it with the loop bound only, leaving two definitions of the listLevel band and one boundary outside the invariant the change defines.

samples.summary: `applyListLevelChanges` is copy-pasted into three editors instead of being a shared helper next to the planner
samples.evidence: The same write loop over `planListLevelChanges(...)` appears three times: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts` (`applyListLevelChanges`, with an extra `markDirty`), `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts` (`private applyListLevelChanges`) and `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts` (`applyListLevelChanges`), each with a near-identical doc comment. The lessons doc's own stated value was that "the rule itself now lives in one pure function" — the planning half is shared, the applying half is not, so the three copies (which already differ in dirty-marking) are the next thing to drift, exactly as the pre-change six handlers did.

samples.summary: Slides PPTX export still hard-codes its own [0, 8] list-level ceiling rather than importing the now-shared `MAX_LIST_LEVEL`
samples.evidence: `listLevelAttr` clamps with a literal `Math.min(8, n)` on the same untrusted `block.listLevel` the docs engine now bands via `normalizeListLevel`/`MAX_LIST_LEVEL` (exported from both `@wafflebase/docs` entries by this diff). The OOXML `ST_TextIndentLevelType` limit happens to coincide with the editor ceiling, so the duplication is benign today, but it is a second literal definition of the same band. The branch's own lessons file records this as knowingly left undone.

samples.summary: Module split rationale does not match the modules: `row-height.ts` is separate "because a gesture plans with them" but contains no planner
samples.evidence: numeric-attrs.ts:4-7 explains that `listLevel` and `rowHeights` get their own modules "because a gesture plans with them. These are only ever read". `list-level.ts` does contain `planListLevelChanges`, but `row-height.ts` holds only `normalizeRowHeight`/`normalizeRowHeights` — read-only, i.e. the same category as `numeric-attrs.ts`. Three near-identical band modules with a rationale that only applies to one of them is arbitrary organization for a reader trying to find where a band lives; `normalizeRowHeight` would sit naturally in `numeric-attrs.ts`.

samples.summary: Design doc says "All six writers route through it" then names seven handlers
samples.evidence: docs.md's new §"Changing a list level carries the subtree" states "All six writers route through it (`handleTab`, `handleIndent`, `handleOutdent` in `text-editor.ts`, and the `indent` / `outdent` API pair in both `editor.ts` and `text-box-editor.ts`...)" — that enumeration is seven handlers (3 + 2 + 2), matching the diff. The task doc phrases it as "four entry points (6 handlers)". A reader auditing coverage against the doc will come up one short.
